Title: Source 4: [Adapted from] The Extermination of the American Bison (1889)
Author: by William T. Homaday
Content: In these `text(days)` of railroads and endless hunting parties, there is no possibility of there being anywhere in the United States a herd of a `text(hundred)`, or even `text(fifty)`, buffaloes. The buffalo provided the Indians with food, clothing, shelter, bedding, saddles, ropes, shields, and numerous smaller articles of use. The Indians of what was `text(once)` the buffalo country are not starving and freezing now. That is because the United States government supplies them regularly with beef and blankets instead of buffalo.
